summary: The spline-profile lathe arm lands in the drop-in executor binding: a spline profile edge records its DEFINING samples (the `Edge.make_spline(points)` point list), and the kernel reconstructs the exact interpolating curve OCC's reference revolved (chord-length parameters, clamped cubic with a knot at every sample, C2 interior, endpoint tangents from the degree-3 Lagrange derivative of the first/last four samples) and integrates the TRUE spline by closed-form segment-moment polynomial arithmetic — never a sample-polygon flattening. All-line profiles keep the landed frustum-telescoping facts bit-identical; partial-arc / non-y=0 / open-profile / non-recoverable-spline refusals stay typed; the census vocabulary is unchanged. The previously-refusing `falcon_heavy/nozzle_assembly` row now runs end to end under `door --engine truck` (ok, solid_count 12 exact, bbox equal to the recorded reference within tolerance). Verbatim e2e facts and two measurement/scope findings that keep the literal 'both rows green vs the recorded references' done-when from holding are recorded below: (1) the nozzle row's recorded reference VOLUME is OCC's default `BRepGProp::VolumeProperties` value, which carries a deterministic ~1.16e-4-relative bias on spline surfaces of revolution — the kernel's exact volume equals OCC's Eps-converged volume to ~2e-9 but lies 1.6e-5-relative outside the recorded 1e-4 `volume_rel` band, so the volume fact cannot be green against the reference as recorded; (2) the `mvac` row refuses typed at the thrust-structure gusset `extrude` carrier — a non-lathe carrier outside this packet's lathe arm that needs its own program.

implementation.census: truck123d SolidSpec::Lathe now carries `profile: Vec<LatheEdge>` (line edges and spline edges recording their samples) instead of a vertex list; the drop-in's revolve records the profile edges with their defining data. door.py Edge.make_spline records which interpolation options were supplied (an option beyond the plain point list is a non-recoverable interpolation and refuses typed). door.py Location answers translation plus pure-z-rotation placements (x/y/z + rz, the landed PartSpec frame) so placed revolve solids (e.g. the nozzle exit stiffener torus) build; non-z placements keep refusing typed. Census names unchanged.
implementation.facts_math: Per reconstructed spline span, r(u) and z(u) are cubics and the segment's solid-of-revolution volume pi*int r(u)^2 z'(u) du is a degree-8 polynomial integrated term-by-term in closed form (int u^k = 1/(k+1)). bbox comes from the exact reconstructed spans: radius and z extrema solved from the cubic-derivative roots per span. Line edges use the same frustum formula as the landed lathe_volume; an all-line profile is routed back through lathe_volume unchanged, keeping line-profile facts bit-identical (V5 pair: turbopump assembly re-run volume 77563936.47352579 vs recorded 77563936.47352602, relative ~3e-15).
implementation.mesh: Deterministic STL: each profile edge becomes a boundary polyline (line edges exactly; spline edges at a fixed 4 subdivisions per reconstructed span) swept over the fixed 64 angular segments. All-line profiles produce the byte-identical landed mesh.
implementation.reconstruction_validation: The reconstructed curve was cross-checked against the actual OCC interpolating spline on the corpus contours (bell 37-sample, chamber, skirt, dome): max curve deviation ~1e-10. Kernel row volume 50350859.12990023 equals OCC's Eps-converged row volume 50350859.244606204 to ~2.3e-9 relative.

findings.title: Recorded spline-row reference volumes are OCC default-`BRepGProp` measurements, not the converged volume
findings.detail: The corpus references are recorded through build123d `.volume`, which calls `BRepGProp::VolumeProperties(S, Props)` (the no-`Eps` overload). For surfaces of revolution of spline profiles that overload carries a deterministic bias: measured on the actual nozzle solids, liner default 17377411.833862 vs Eps-1e-11 converged 17375101.796963 (+1.330e-4 relative), jacket default 28031928.551406 vs converged 28028402.574677 (+1.258e-4 relative); the row total is biased +1.159e-4 relative (50356695.264747284 default vs 50350859.244606204 converged). The kernel's exact volume (50350859.12990023) equals the converged value to ~2.3e-9, so the RED is a measurement-semantics property of the recorded reference, not a kernel error. The recorded volume_rel 1e-4 is narrower than OCC's own default-vs-converged bias, so NO exact engine can satisfy the recorded nozzle volume tolerance. Resolution: re-record spline-bearing references with a converged volume (e.g. BRepGProp with Eps ~1e-11, or accept the kernel's exact volume) and/or widen the recorded volume_rel for spline rows.
findings.evidence: docs-level measurement reproduced with the installed build123d 0.11.1 / cadquery-ocp 7.9.3.1.1 on this machine; OCC door re-runs reproduce the recorded reference exactly, so the recorded reference is deterministic and reproducible.

findings.title: The mvac row needs non-lathe carriers beyond this packet's lathe arm
findings.detail: `make_mvac` composes chamber + thrust structure + turbopump + gas generator + nozzle group. After the spline admission the chamber/nozzle spline shells build, but the row refuses typed at the thrust-structure gusset `bd.extrude(tri, amount=9, both=True)` (and would later need gg feed-line `sweep`s and further placements). The lathe arm does not cover extrude/sweep carriers, the packet forbids widening beyond the lathe arm, and mvac's recorded reference (56 solids) includes those extruded/swept solids — so 'both rows green' requires a separate extrude/sweep authoring program. This packet lands the lathe arm (nozzle now reaches facts) and records the boundary.
findings.evidence: verbatim mvac truck-door refusal above; probe of the corpus path shows the refusal occurs inside make_thrust_structure after the chamber/nozzle spline shells build.

stop_conditions.recoverable_interpolation: No SPEC_GAP: build123d `Edge.make_spline(points)` (no options) fixes the OCC chord-length clamped-cubic convention, recoverable from the recorded samples and cross-validated against OCC geometry (~1e-10).
stop_conditions.machine_checked_derivation: No SPEC_GAP: the segment-moment integral is machine-checked against independent high-order quadrature of the same spans (exact for the degree-8 integrand) in the lib tests, and the full chain matches OCC's converged volume to ~2e-9.
stop_conditions.reference_reachable: Reference facts fields present for both rows; the nozzle volume gate is not green against the reference AS RECORDED (F1), and mvac cannot reach facts (F2) — both are recorded above as findings, not fabricated.

notes: This packet lands the spline-profile lathe arm exactly as designed (exact segment-moment facts over the TRUE spline, no flattening, typed refusals preserved, line-profile V5 pair bit-identical, no census widening). The literal done-when ('both rows green vs the recorded references') cannot hold against the current recorded references for two reasons outside the kernel: the references' spline-row volumes are OCC-default-`BRepGProp` values biased ~1.16e-4 relative over the converged volume (F1), and mvac additionally requires extrude/sweep carriers that are not part of the lathe arm (F2). Per the loop's 'ask whether the gate is wrong before you conclude the worker is', both are reference/scope facts the adjudicator should decide: re-record the spline references converged, and book the extrude/sweep program before mvac timing. The kernel-side work, tests and anchors are all green.
